- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.30) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is positive and forecast is trending up, cap the 30-day forecast at +10% above recent 10-day average to prevent overreaction.  
- If last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive downward moves), model should not forecast further decline; instead, slightly bias upward toward prior 10-day mean.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, avoid forecasting sharp upward moves; use 10-day moving average as baseline for 30-day projection.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates true price by >2% over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for the next 3 days to correct for lagged bias.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, model should not forecast a 30-day peak higher than 1.5x the 10-day high — avoid “over-optimism” in bullish sentiment.
